summary: PulseGuard v0.6.19 fixes the post-scan BIOS notification callback, restores an even Optimize Process/Changes layout, and prevents duplicate interactive launches from colliding with the updater.

sections.heading: BIOS notification callback exception fixed
sections.detail: The post-Full-Health-Scan and post-Fix-All BIOS notification no longer uses a GetNewClosure WinForms callback that could lose script function resolution and throw a .NET 'Write-Log is not recognized' exception. The queued prompt now runs in the normal PulseGuard script context, and callback logging is non-fatal.

sections.heading: Optimize upper deck returned to half-and-half
sections.detail: Optimization Process and Changes Recorded now split the available upper row evenly, with Changes Recorded taking the exact remainder. The hologram remains inside the Process panel without allowing that panel to dominate the row.

sections.heading: Duplicate PulseGuard windows blocked
sections.detail: The interactive app now owns a named single-instance mutex. The launcher checks the same mutex before running the updater, so a minimized/open PulseGuard window causes the second launch to stop with a clear message instead of attempting an update against files already in use. Worker and scheduled-scan processes remain independent.

sections.heading: v0.6.18 health findings preserved
sections.detail: The v0.6.18 report correctly identifies BIOS 1078 with stable 1681 available, keeps ASUS DriverHub browser-only, reports zero Device Manager issues, and marks retained shutdown/crash evidence as Monitoring rather than a current active failure.
